statement: Jabir: in the tenth year it was announced he would perform hajj; many came to Madinah wishing to follow him; Jabir saw riders and walkers as far as the eye could see before him, to his right, left and behind.
notes: Direct speech. From the long hadith of Jabir; the Arafah sermon portion was machine-checked in the Muslim dataset (no. 2951); this opening is from memory. Abd al-Baqi number from memory.

statement: It was his only hajj after the Hijrah; afterwards he returned to Madinah.
He said: learn your rites from me, for I do not know whether I will perform hajj after this.
notes: Direct speech. Content machine-checked in the Muslim dataset (no. 3137); Abd al-Baqi number from memory. Said on the day of sacrifice while stoning.

statement: The sermon at Arafah: sanctity of blood and property; everything of Jahiliyyah abolished, its blood-feuds and its usury, beginning with the usury of al-Abbas; fear Allah regarding women, their rights to provision and clothing; the Book of Allah left among them.
notes: Direct speech, abridged. Machine-checked against the dataset text. Omitted: the first blood-claim abolished (Ibn Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith), and the passage on husbands' rights and discipline. Reviewer to confirm the abridgement is fair.

statement: He said they would be asked about him; they testified that he had conveyed, fulfilled and counselled; he raised his finger to the sky and pointed it at the people saying 'O Allah, bear witness' three times.
Umar: a Jew said they would have taken the day of that verse as a festival; Umar said it was revealed to the Prophet standing at Arafah on a Friday.

notes: Paraphrase of meaning (part of the verse).

statement: Abu Bakrah: the sermon on the day of sacrifice at Mina: the questions about the day, month and land; sanctity of blood, property and honour until they meet their Lord; 'have I conveyed?'; 'O Allah bear witness'; let the present inform the absent; do not revert to disbelief striking one another's necks.
notes: Direct speech, abridged. Machine-checked for the opening of each narration; the later sentences are from memory of the same narrations.

statement: Ibn Umar: we used to speak of the Farewell Hajj while the Prophet was among us and did not know what the farewell meant.
notes: Machine-checked. The well-known words 'no Arab has superiority over a non-Arab...' (Musnad Ahmad, sahih) are not included; reviewer may wish to add them with their reference.
